summary: Baie-Johan-Beetz Water Aerodrome (YBJ) is a small seaplane base serving the remote coastal village of Baie-Johan-Beetz on Quebec's Côte-Nord (North Shore) along the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The community, named after a 19th-century Belgian-born settler, relies heavily on air access given its isolation and limited road infrastructure. The aerodrome primarily supports scheduled and charter floatplane services connecting the village to larger regional hubs.
faqs:
Q: What type of facility is Baie-Johan-Beetz Water Aerodrome?
A: It is a seaplane base (water aerodrome), meaning aircraft land and take off from the surface of the adjacent bay rather than a conventional runway.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to YBJ?
A: Scheduled floatplane service is typically operated by regional carriers serving the Côte-Nord communities, though schedules and operators may change seasonally.

Q: Is the aerodrome open year-round?
A: Operations are generally seasonal and weather-dependent, as the bay can freeze in winter, which may limit or suspend floatplane access.

Q: Are there customs or immigration facilities at YBJ?
A: No, this is a small domestic seaplane base without customs or immigration services; it handles local and regional flights only.
transport_tips: There is no fixed terminal building; passengers typically check in directly at the dock or shoreline before boarding. Ground transportation options in Baie-Johan-Beetz are extremely limited, so arranging any onward travel needs in advance is advisable. The nearest larger communities with road connections and full services are accessible primarily via the ferry network along the North Shore or by continuing onward by air.
local_tip: Floatplane schedules on the Côte-Nord are heavily weather-dependent, so build flexibility into your travel plans and always confirm your flight the morning of departure—delays of several hours are not uncommon when fog or wind picks up over the Gulf.
